title: SRE: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks
author: Ariana Chen
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling recommendations, and canonical runbooks. It is intended for SREs, production engineers, on-call responders, and product owners who share responsibility for the availability, latency, and efficiency of inference services.

Scope:
- Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints (Redwood API hosted), Dedicated control plane, and the internal control services that impact customer-facing SLOs (routing, auth, quota).
- Excludes model training pipelines and non-customer-facing batch analytics jobs (covered by eng-infra policy).

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

1.1 SLO categories (examples):
- Availability SLO (customer-visible): percentage of successful 2xx responses for production inference endpoints per calendar month.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 request-to-first-token (RTFT) and request-to-last-token (RTLT) for common request classes (chat, streaming, embeddings).
- Correctness / Quality SLOs: end-to-end accuracy or task-specific metrics tracked via eval harness and periodic regression tests.

1.2 Canonical SLO targets (baseline; product teams may tighten after risk review):
| Service tier | Availability (monthly) | p95 RTFT | p99 RTFT | Notes |
| Hosted API - standard | 99.95% | 200 ms | 500 ms | Applies to text generation 0-2k token responses |
| Hosted API - embeddings | 99.90% | 150 ms | 400 ms | Short model inference path |
| Dedicated (reserved) | 99.99% | 150 ms | 350 ms | SLA-backed commit required |

1.3 Error budget policy:
- Error budget = (1 - SLO) * window (monthly). For 99.95% SLO, monthly budget = 0.05% of requests.
- Automatic actions by error budget burn rate:
  - Green (0-25% burn): normal operations.
  - Yellow (25-75% burn): notify product & infra; postpone non-essential releases; run focused incident drills if trend persists for 24h.
  - Red (>=75% burn or projected exhaustion in 24h): immediate release freeze for non-critical changes, escalate to SRE on-call lead, convene outage review and capacity mobilization.
- Ownership: product-PO owns SLO targets; SRE owns measurement, dashboards, and enforcing error budget controls.

1.4 Measurement and measurement windows:
- Primary measurement: monthly rolling window, reported daily. 7-day and 30-day views shown in dashboards.
- Metrics sources: gateway logs (api-gateway), runtime telemetry (runtime-metrics), and edge proxies. Aggregation pipeline: logs -> kinesis -> metrics service -> SLO backend.
- Error classes counted: 5xx HTTP codes, 4xx from quota/auth errors are excluded from availability SLO but included in customer-impact dashboards.

2) Incident Review Standards

2.1 Triage timelines and roles:
- Sev definitions (aligned to company oncall taxonomy): Sev-1 (platform down / major customer impact), Sev-2 (degraded but functional), Sev-3 (minor).
- Timeline expectations: acknowledge within 5 minutes for Sev-1, preliminary incident timeline within 1 hour, RCA assigned within 24 hours.
- Incident roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications lead, Tech lead, Scribe, Postmortem owner. Roster maintained in oncall rota doc.

2.2 Post-incident review (PIR) template (minimum):
- Title, impact window, services affected, customer impact summary (who/what/how many), timeline of events, root cause analysis, corrective actions (short/medium/long-term), follow-up owners and ETA, severity classification, and learnings.
- PIR must be published to Confluence within 7 business days for Sev-1/2 and within 14 days for Sev-3.
- Follow-up verification: owners must provide verification evidence (metrics, deployment IDs) when marking corrective actions complete.

2.3 RCA standards and blameless language:
- Focus on systems and process fixes; avoid attributing root cause to individual human error.
- Require hypothesis testing: every root cause claim must include evidence (logs, spans, config diffs, test results).

3) Capacity Planning

3.1 Capacity targets and safety margins:
- Target utilization: 60% steady-state utilization per GPU cluster to preserve headroom for spikes (target range 50-70%).
- Peak scaling policy: autoscale to 85% utilization threshold, soft-limit autoscaling at 90%, hard caps defined by budget/region.
- Warm pool target: maintain 10-15% of capacity as warm spare across regions to enable fast scale-ups.

3.2 Demand forecasting and cadence:
- Quarterly capacity review led by eng-sre with inputs from product (usage forecasts), sales (committed Dedicated capacity), and infra (available hardware).
- Monthly run-rate review: compare actual requests, token counts, and instance-hours vs. forecasts; adjust procurement or cloud pledges as needed.
- Spike-run simulation: at least one game-day per quarter simulating 2x sustained load for 30 minutes with degraded components to validate autoscaling and fallbacks.

3.3 Provisioning checklist (abbreviated):
1. Validate forecast inputs and model mix (chat vs. embed).
2. Confirm regional distribution and capacity constraints (GPU types: A100, H100, L4).
3. Provision warm pool and autoscaling policies in terraform; create PR and run canary deploy.
4. Update dashboards and runbook thresholds; notify oncall.

4) Reliability Initiatives and SLIs

- Prioritized initiatives (rolling 12 months):
  1) Reduce p99 RTFT by 30% via kernel & KV-cache optimizations. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
  2) Implement prefix caching for common prompts to reduce token cost and latency. Owner: eng-platform.
  3) Automatic model fallback routing to compatible variants when primary model is overloaded. Owner: runtime-routing.
  4) Improve SLO detection fidelity by instrumenting end-to-end traces in the frontend gateway. Owner: eng-sre.

- SLIs to be maintained in dashboards:
  - availability.success_rate (1m/5m/30m windows), request.latency.p95, request.latency.p99, kvcache.hit_rate, batch.size.avg.

5) Operational Tooling and Dashboards

- Required dashboards (minimum):
  - SLO overview (per service, per region, error budget burn charts).
  - Latency heatmap (p50/p95/p99 by endpoint and model).
  - Capacity view (utilization, cluster headroom, warm pool sizes, autoscale events).
  - Error taxonomy (5xx by code, upstream errors, OOMs, rate limits).
- Tooling stack recommendations:
  - Metrics & alerts: Prometheus + Cortex for long-term metrics, Grafana for dashboards, Alertmanager for paging.
  - Tracing: Jaeger/OTel collector, traces linked to dashboards via trace_id.
  - Logs: structured logs shipped to Elasticsearch or Loki; alertable log patterns for high-rate error spikes.
  - SLO engine: internal SLO service (slo-service) that consumes metrics and computes burn rates; exposes REST endpoints for policy enforcement.

6) Canonical Runbooks (templates + example)

6.1 Runbook template (single-runbook per page):
- Runbook title (service)
- Pager signal(s) and severity mapping
- Quick-checks (2-4 bullet checks to assess health)
- Mitigation steps (ordered, numbered)
- Rollback / mitigation commands (shell/cli snippets)
- Owner and escalation path
- Post-incident steps and verification

6.2 Example: "inference-gateway 5xx spike"
Quick checks:
1. Check SLO dashboard - current error budget burn and 5xx trend (grafana/slo-overview).
2. Check gateway logs: errors per 1m (loki query).
3. Check backend runtime cluster health (k8s pods, GPU utilization).

Mitigation steps (ordered):
1. If error rate > 2% of traffic and rising, enable rate-limiting rule for anonymous requests (cli: redwoodctl policies enable rate-limit --policy anon-shield).
2. If gateway processes show OOMs, scale gateway deployment by +2 replicas and restart crashlooping pods (k apply --replicas=+2).
3. If backend inference nodes show high GPU memory OOMs, switch heavy models to queued mode and divert new requests to lighter model variants via runtime-routing: set route weight primary=0.7 fallback=0.3.
4. If sustained degradation > 30 minutes, escalate to SRE on-call lead and open incident.

Rollback/verification:
- After mitigation, verify p95/p99 trending back to baseline for 30 minutes before re-enabling suppressed traffic.
- Document all actions (deployment IDs, commands run) in the incident ticket.

7) On-call and Roster Practices

- Primary on-call responsibilities: monitor SLOs, respond to pages within defined acknowledgment times, execute runbooks, and own incident postmortems.
- Rotation: weekly primary rotation with a 2-week secondary rotation. SRE lead maintains shift calendar.
- Escalation: 15 minutes escalation window for unresolved Sev-1; follow contact matrix in oncall roster.

8) Governance and Change Controls

- SLO changes: any change to SLO targets must be approved by product-PO and SRE lead, and documented with rationale and rollback plan.
- Release freeze policy: when error budget is in Red, a temporary release freeze is enacted for non-critical changes; exemptions require SRE lead approval.

9) Metrics, Reporting, and Audits

- Weekly SLO report delivered to Product and Execs summarizing burn rates, recent incidents, and planned mitigations.
- Quarterly reliability review with product and sales to align SLAs and capacity commitments.
- Audit trail: all oncall actions and runbook executions must be referenced by ticket IDs and stored in incident tracker for 365 days.

Appendix A - Useful Commands and Queries:
- Check SLO burn (curl): curl -sS https://slo-service.internal/api/v1/burn?service=inference-gateway&window=30d | jq
- Query p99 latency (prometheus): sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
- Loki example (5xx): {job="api-gateway"} |= "HTTP/1.1 5" | count_over_time({job="api-gateway"}[1m])

Appendix B - Ownership matrix (examples):
- inference-gateway: owner eng-platform, secondary eng-sre
- runtime-nodes: owner eng-serving-runtime
- slo-service: owner eng-sre

Document maintenance:
- This page is reviewed quarterly by eng-sre; reviewers list above will be notified for major changes.
